{{Short description|Indian industrialist and philanthropist (born 1957)}} {{Use Indian English|date=February 2023}} {{Use dmy dates|date=February 2023}} {{Infobox person | name = Sunil Mittal | image = Sunil Mittal.jpg | caption = Sunil Mittal in 2024 | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|df=y|1957|10|23}} | birth_place = [[Ludhiana]], [[East Punjab|Punjab]], India | occupation = {{hlist|[[Industrialist]]|[[philanthropist]]}} | title = Founder and chairman [[Bharti Enterprises]] | spouse = Nyna Mittal | children = 3 (including [[Kavin Bharti Mittal|Kavin]] and Shravin) | parents = | father = [[Sat Pal Mittal]] | relatives = [[Sharan Pasricha]]
(son-in-law) | alma_mater = [[Panjab University, Chandigarh|Punjab University]] ([[Bachelor of Arts|BA]]) | awards = [[Padma Bhushan]] (2007), [[Order of the British Empire|KBE]] (2024) }} '''Sunil Bharti Mittal''' (born 23 October 1957) is an Indian entrepreneur and philanthropist. He is the Founder and Chairman of [[Bharti Enterprises]], a conglomerate with interests in telecommunications, satellite communications, digital infrastructure, financial services, real estate, and hospitality.{{Cite news |last=Jolly |first=Jasper |date=2024-08-12 |title=Sunil Bharti Mittal: who is the Indian tycoon now BT’s largest shareholder? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/article/2024/aug/12/sunil-bharti-mittal-india-telecoms-bt |access-date=2026-05-04 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}} Its flagship company, [[Bharti Airtel]], operates in 17 countries across India, South Asia and Africa{{Cite web |date=2026-03-28 |title=How Sunil Mittal’s Bharti Enterprises is orchestrating a textbook succession – BusinessToday |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/how-sunil-mittals-bharti-enterprises-is-orchestrating-a-textbook-succession-522833-2026-03-28 |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=Business Today |language=en}} and is the world's second-largest mobile operator by subscriber base.{{Cite news |last=Mallick |first=Subhrojit |date=2026-04-02 |title=Airtel hits 650 million users, becomes world's No. 2 telecom operator |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/telecom-news/airtel-becomes-worlds-second-largest-mobile-service-provider-with-650-million-subscribers/articleshow/129972236.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-05-04 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} In 2024, Bharti Airtel became the first Indian company of its generation to reach a market capitalisation of US$100 billion.{{Cite journal |last=Banik |first=Arindam |last2=Nag |first2=Tirthankar |date=2016-12-01 |title=Bharti Airtel and Zain: A Journey into New Territories |url=https://doi.org/10.1177/0972150916660647 |journal=Global Business Review |language=EN |volume=17 |issue=6 |pages=1516–1521 |doi=10.1177/0972150916660647 |issn=0972-1509|url-access=subscription }} Mittal also serves as the Co-Chairman of [[Eutelsat]] and is a Director on the board of [[BT Group]] Plc. He has held various roles in several business and industry bodies. He was the Chaiman of the [[International Chamber of Commerce]] from 2016 to 2018{{Cite news |date=2018-06-21 |title=Sunil Mittal becomes honorary chairman of International Chamber of Commerce |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/sunil-mittal-becomes-honorary-chairman-of-international-chamber-of-commerce/articleshow/64683589.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2024-03-22 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}In March 2026, Mittal received the GSMA Lifetime Achievement Award at Mobile World Congress Barcelona.{{cite news |date=March 2, 2026 |title=Bharti Airtel founder receives GSMA honour |url=https://www.news9live.com/technology/tech-news/bharti-airtel-founder-sunil-mittal-receives-gsmas-highest-honour-at-mwc-2026-2938189 |work=News9live}} and the [[GSMA|GSM Association]] from 2017 to 2018. Between 2009 and 2021, he served as a trustee of the [[Carnegie Endowment for International Peace]]. During India's [[G20]] presidency in 2023, he chaired the B20 Action Council on African Economic Integration. His additional board and advisory roles include membership in the [[World Economic Forum]]'s International Business Council, Hakluyt's International Advisory Board, and the Global Board of Advisors at the [[Council on Foreign Relations]]. He has previously served on the boards of [[Unilever]], [[Standard Chartered]], and [[SoftBank Group|SoftBank Corp]]. Mittal currently holds Co-Chair positions at the India-UK CEO Forum and is a Co-Anchor of the ICT and Emerging Technologies & Digital Infrastructure working group of the India–US CEO Forum. Earlier, he was the President of the [[Confederation of Indian Industry]] (2007–2008) and a member of the Prime Minister of India's Council on Trade and Industry (2004–2014). He was awarded the [[Padma Bhushan]] by the [[Government of India]] in 2007.{{cite web |date=27 January 2009 |title=Sunil Mittal, Indra Nooyi get Padma Bhushan |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/bline/2007/01/27/stories/2007012702200700.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120912214846/http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/bline/2007/01/27/stories/2007012702200700.htm |archive-date=12 September 2012 |access-date=1 April 2010 |work=Business Line}} In 2024, he was appointed an honorary [[Order of the British Empire|Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (KBE) by H.M. King [[Charles III]],{{Cite web |title=Honorary Knighthood medal presented to Sunil Bharti Mittal |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/news/honorary-knighthood-medal-presented-to-sunil-bharti-mittal |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=GOV.UK |language=en}} becoming the first Indian citizen to receive the honour from the King.{{Cite web |last=Chakraborty |first=Subhayan |date=28 February 2024 |title=Sunil Bharti Mittal conferred honorary knighthood by King Charles III |url=https://www.business-standard.com/india-news/bharti-enterprise-chairman-sunil-bharti-mittal-knighted-by-king-charles-iii-124022801029_1.html |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=Business Standard}} == Early life and education == Mittal was born in 1957 in [[Ludhiana]], Punjab.{{cite news |title=Lunch with Rajan Bharti Mittal |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/the-leisure-lounge/lunch-with-rajan-bharti-mittal/articleshow/3150529.cms?from=mdr |publisher=economictimes.com}} His father, [[Sat Pal Mittal|Sat Paul Mittal]], was a politician who served three terms as a member of the [[Rajya Sabha]] between 1976 and 1992,{{cite news |last1=Nair |first1=Vinod |date=22 December 2002 |title=Sunil Mittal speaking: I started with a dream |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshow/msid-32019056,prtpage-1.cms |work=The Times of India}} and received the United Nations Peace Medal in 1987 from Secretary-General Javier Pérez de Cuéllar for his work in population control, development, and world peace. Sunil Mittal attended school in Punjab, including a period at [[Wynberg Allen School]] in Mussoorie,{{cite book |last=Mittal |first=Airtel |title=Pesu! |date=July 2008 |publisher=Kizhakku |isbn=978-81-8368-864-2 |edition=Tamil |page=14}} and graduated with a Bachelor of Arts from [[Panjab University]] in 1976.{{Cite web |date=2016-05-26 |title=Sunil B. Mittal, OPM 27, 1999 |url=https://www.alumni.hbs.edu/stories/Pages/story-bulletin.aspx?num=5600 |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=Harvard Business School Alumni |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Sunil Bharti Mittal - Creating Emerging Markets - Harvard Business School |url=https://www.hbs.edu/creating-emerging-markets/interviews/Pages/profile.aspx?profile=smittal |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=www.hbs.edu}} == Career == === 1976–1989: Early ventures === Mittal began his career in 1976, founding Bharti Enterprises with a ₹20,000 investment to manufacture bicycle crankshafts in Ludhiana.{{Cite web |last=Munjal |first=Dr Pawan |date=2021-08-21 |title=Sunil Bharti Mittal: First mover |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/independence-day-special/story/20210830-sunil-bharti-mittal-first-mover-1843115-2021-08-20 |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=India Today |language=en}}{{cite web |title=Sunil Mittal TimesNow interview |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NU39b9g1oOo |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140706081032/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NU39b9g1oOo |archive-date=2014-07-06 |access-date=1 April 2010 |via=YouTube}} He subsequently diversified into the production of shoddy yarn and stainless steel sheets.{{cite news |author=Clay Chandler |date=17 January 2007 |title=Wireless Wonder: India's Sunil Mittal |url=https://money.cnn.com/magazines/fortune/fortune_archive/2007/01/22/8397979/index2.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071130062303/https://money.cnn.com/magazines/fortune/fortune_archive/2007/01/22/8397979/index2.htm |archive-date=2007-11-30 |access-date=1 April 2010 |publisher=CNN}} In 1980, he established Bharti Overseas Trading Company to import industrial materials and consumer products{{cite book |last=Mittal |first=Airtel |title=Pesu! |date=July 2008 |publisher=Kizhakku |isbn=978-81-8368-864-2 |edition=Tamil |page=14}} and in 1981, began importing and distributing Suzuki portable generators. This business ceased in 1983 following government restrictions on generator imports.{{cite web |title=Sunil Mittal TimesNow interview |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NU39b9g1oOo |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140706081032/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NU39b9g1oOo |archive-date=2014-07-06 |access-date=1 April 2010 |via=YouTube}}{{Cite web |date=18 February 2015 |title=40 years ago... And now: Sunil Mittal - One step ahead of reforms |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/40-years-ago-and-now-sunil-mittal-one-step-ahead-of-reforms-115021800032_1.html |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=Business Standard}}{{Cite news |last=Tyagi |first=Chhavi |date=2017-12-16 |title=How Bharti Airtel's Sunil Mittal was once in financial crisis for the want of Rs 5000 |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/small-biz/startups/newsbuzz/how-bharti-airtels-sunil-mittal-was-once-in-financial-crisis-for-the-want-of-rs-5000/articleshow/62093302.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-05-04 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} In the mid-1980s, Mittal transitioned to the telecommunications sector after identifying a market for push-button telephones, which were then uncommon in India.{{cite web |title=Sunil Mittal TimesNow interview |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NU39b9g1oOo |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140706081032/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NU39b9g1oOo |archive-date=2014-07-06 |access-date=1 April 2010 |via=YouTube}} Initially he imported kits for local assembly and introduced India's first push-button phones under the "Mitbrau" brand. He subsequently founded Bharti Telecom Limited (BTL) in 1985. Through a technical partnership with [[Siemens AG]], the company began manufacturing electronic push-button phones under the "Beetel" brand.{{cite book |last=Mittal |first=Airtel |title=Pesu! |date=July 2008 |publisher=Kizhakku |isbn=978-81-8368-864-2 |edition=Tamil |page=14}} By 1989, BTL had established a manufacturing facility in Ludhiana and had become one of India's largest domestic telephone producers, with an annual capacity of 200,000 units.{{Cite web |last=Goyal |first=Vivek LawMalini |date=2002-02-25 |title=How Sunil Bharti Mittal built his telecom empire |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/economy/story/20020225-how-sunil-bharti-mittal-built-his-telecom-empire-795970-2002-02-24 |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=India Today |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=I was the first one to make push button phones in India: Sunil Bharti Mittal |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/anniversary/story/20210104-i-was-the-first-one-to-make-push-button-phones-in-india-1753031-2020-12-27 |website=India Today}} === 1990–2009: Telecommunications and diversification === In 1990, Bharti expanded its equipment manufacturing through partnerships with [[LG|Lucky Goldstar]] and Takacom to produce cordless phones and answering machines, through its Beetel brand. {{Cite web |last=Ghosh |first=Leslie D'Monte |date=2014-07-16 |title=Bharti cuts a connection to the past as telecom biz evolves |url=https://www.livemint.com/Industry/rIwf13ZjIHuMi0S52FyfUO/Bharti-cuts-a-connection-to-the-past-as-telecom-biz-evolves.html |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=mint |language=en}}The company shifted toward telecommunications services in 1992, forming a consortium with [[SFR]], Emtel, and MSI to bid for mobile licenses in Indian metropolitan circles.{{cite news |last1=Nair |first1=Vinod |date=22 December 2002 |title=Sunil Mittal speaking: I started with a dream |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshow/msid-32019056,prtpage-1.cms |work=The Times of India}}{{cite web |title=Sunil Mittal TimesNow interview |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NU39b9g1oOo |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140706081032/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NU39b9g1oOo |archive-date=2014-07-06 |access-date=1 April 2010 |via=YouTube}} Following the grant of a license, Bharti launched [[GSM]] services in Delhi in 1995 under the [[Bharti Airtel|Airtel]] brand. The company's international expansion began in 1998 with the launch of mobile services in the [[Seychelles]]. Singtel acquired a stake in Bharti for US$400 million in 2000, which coincided with the launch of the "IndiaOne" service to reduce long-distance tariffs.{{cite web |title=Sunil Mittal TimesNow interview |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NU39b9g1oOo |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140706081032/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NU39b9g1oOo |archive-date=2014-07-06 |access-date=1 April 2010 |via=YouTube}} In February 2002, Bharti went public and launched India's first 100% book-built initial public offering (IPO); around the same time its mobile subscriber base reached two million. During this period, the company expanded beyond voice services into data and enterprise sectors and introduced BlackBerry to the Indian market.{{Cite news |date=2004-10-20 |title=AirTel launches Blackberry handsets |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/communicators-the-mittals/bharti-televenture/airtel-launches-blackberry-handsets/articleshow/950209.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-05-04 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} In 2004, Bharti Airtel entered a landmark outsourcing model partnering with [[IBM]] and [[Ericsson]],{{Cite web |date=2014-05-29 |title=Bharti Airtel's evolving outsourcing strategy |url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/v0BPytPnOJMAalnMRWRDAM/Bharti-Airtels-evolving-outsourcing-strategy.html |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=mint |language=en}} for network management, enabling it to scale rapidly while focusing on its core business. By 2005, Airtel was operational in all 23 Indian telecom circles.{{Cite web |date=2008-03-05 |title=Bharti Airtel Rider of the boom - BusinessToday |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/cover-story/story/bharti-airtel-rider-of-the-boom-129561-2008-03-05 |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=Business Today |language=en}} In 2007, Bharti partnered with Walmart to enter the Indian retail market{{cite magazine |title=Wal-Mart May Open India Retail Stores Within Two Years |url=http://www.businessweek.com/news/2012-09-21/wal-mart-in-talks-with-bharti-after-india-eases-rules |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120924205229/http://www.businessweek.com/news/2012-09-21/wal-mart-in-talks-with-bharti-after-india-eases-rules |archive-date=24 September 2012 |access-date=5 April 2013 |magazine=Bloomberg Businessweek}} and established the financial services venture Bharti [[Axa|AXA]]. That same year, the group reached the 50 million customer milestone, becoming one of the top five mobile operators globally.{{Cite news |last=Philip |first=Nandini Sengupta & Joji Thomas |date=2007-10-19 |title=Meet the lord of the rings Sunil Mittal |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/meet-the-lord-of-the-rings-sunil-mittal/articleshow/2472183.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-05-04 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} Bharti Infratel was formed as a subsidiary for tower infrastructure in 2007. In 2012, Mittal took Bharti Infratel public, raising $760 million. This entity later in 2020 merged [[Indus Towers]] to create a mega tower company, along with [[Vodafone|Vodafone Group]].{{Cite web |last=Jayaram |first=Anup |date=2022-09-12 |title=Sunil Mittal: Riding The Waves |url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/long-reads/sunil-mittal-riding-the-waves/109629 |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=Fortune India |language=en}} The UK Group held 28.12% stake, while Bharti Airtel owned 36.7%. In 2008 and 2009, Mittal entered two rounds of merger negotiations with South Africa's [[MTN Group]], although, the discussions did not culminate in a deal. During the same period, Bharti Airtel continued to strengthen its international presence and, in 2009, launched its 2G and 3G services in Sri Lanka.{{Cite web |date=2009-01-12 |title=Bharti Airtel starts mobile services in Sri Lanka |url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/S8j8b6egWOXCKCOdBMslrO/Bharti-Airtel-starts-mobile-services-in-Sri-Lanka.html |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=mint |language=en}} === 2010–2019: Global scaling and legal proceedings === In 2010, Bharti acquired [[Zain Group]]'s mobile operations in 15 African countries for US$10.7 billion{{cite news |date=8 June 2010 |title=Bharti completes acquisition of Zain's Africa biz for $10.7bn |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/Bharti-completes-acquisition-of-Zains-Africa-biz-for-10-7bn/articleshow/6023848.cms |access-date=12 November 2015 |work=The Times of India}}{{Cite web |title=Sunil Bharti Mittal: The man who transformed India's telecom sector is the Business Icon of the Year; here's why |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/interactive/photo-essay/sunil-bharti-mittal-the-man-who-transformed-india-s-telecom-sector-is-the-business-icon-of-the-year-heres-why-185-09-03-2024 |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=businesstoday |language=en}} and acquired a 70% stake in Bangladesh's Warid Telecom. In 2013, the India retail partnership with Walmart was dissolved due to regulatory challenges.{{Cite web |title=Damage control: Decoding why Bharti-Walmart love affair ended |url=https://www.firstpost.com/business/damage-control-decoding-why-bharti-walmart-love-affair-ended-1159283.html}} In the same year, Bharti Airtel acquired Warid Congo{{Cite news |last=Philip |first=Joji Thomas |date=2010-01-12 |title=Bharti acquires 70% stake in Warid Telecom |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/bharti-acquires-70-stake-in-warid-telecom/articleshow/5434989.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-05-04 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}{{Cite news |title=India's Airtel continues Africa push with deal in Congo |url=https://www.ft.com/content/829a9bd7-1709-316a-b56c-930027aaa721 |access-date=13 August 2017 |work=Financial Times}}{{subscription required}} and established Nxtra Data Limited as its data-center arm.{{Cite web |title=Airtel Nxtra Data raises 1 billion dollars to power Indias AI data boo |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/news/airtel-draws-1-billion-for-data-centre-arm-nxtra/2992685/1 |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=www.forbesindia.com |language=en}} That same year, Mittal was asked to appear before a Delhi court in connection with an investigation into spectrum allocations. The summon was subsequently quashed by the Supreme Court. By 2015, Bharti Airtel was the third-largest mobile operator globally by subscriber base.{{Cite web |title=Airtel becomes third largest mobile operator globally |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/airtel-becomes-third-largest-mobile-operator-globally-115063000424_1.html}} That year, Bharti became a founding investor in OneWeb, acquiring a strategic minority stake as part of a global consortium.{{Cite news |date=2015-06-26 |title=Bharti Enterprises buys into OneWeb, aims to bring Internet to rural areas via satellites |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/bharti-enterprises-buys-into-oneweb-aims-to-bring-internet-to-rural-areas-via-satellites/articleshow/47815759.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-05-04 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} In 2016, Airtel Payments Bank became the first entity in India to receive a payments bank license from the Reserve Bank of India.{{Cite web |title=Bharti Airtel rolls out India’s first payments bank |url=https://www.vccircle.com/bharti-airtel-rolls-out-indias-first-payments-bank |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=VCCircle |language=en-US}} In 2019, Airtel Africa completed a dual listing - on the London and Nigerian Stock Exchanges. It alsoraised US$3.6 billion through a rights issue.{{Cite journal |last=Banik |first=Arindam |last2=Nag |first2=Tirthankar |date= |title=Bharti Airtel and Zain: A Journey into New Territories |url=https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0972150916660643 |journal=Global Business Review |language=en |volume=17 |issue=6 |pages=1510–1515 |doi=10.1177/0972150916660643 |issn=0972-1509|url-access=subscription }} === 2020–present: Recent developments === Following OneWeb’s 2020 bankruptcy filing, Mittal led a successful US$1 billion consortium with the UK government to acquire the company and later became its Executive Chairman.{{Cite news |date=2020-11-20 |title=OneWeb satellite internet company is officially reborn |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-55016402 |access-date=2026-05-04 |language=en-GB}} Under his leadership, OneWeb completed its LEO satellite constellation via launches using Russian Soyuz flights and a rocket from the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).{{Cite web |title=सुनील मित्तल बोले: भारतीय जमीन से सैटेलाइट लॉन्च करने वाली पहली निजी कंपनी होगी वनवेब |url=https://www.amarujala.com/technology/tech-diary/sunil-bharti-mittal-says-oneweb-to-be-first-private-company-to-launch-satellite-from-indian-soil |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=Amar Ujala |language=hi}} In 2023, OneWeb merged with Eutelsat, with Bharti as the largest shareholder and Mittal as Co-Chair.{{Cite web |last=Aulakh |first=Gulveen |date=2023-09-28 |title=OneWeb set to offer services in India soon as Eutelsat-OneWeb merger finalised {{!}} Company Business News |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/oneweb-set-to-offer-services-in-india-soon-as-eutelsat-oneweb-merger-finalised-11695906560581.html |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=mint |language=en}} That year, Bharti consolidated its insurance business by acquiring AXA's 49% stake, making Bharti Life Ventures Private Limited (BLVPL) the sole owner of the company. As of 2026, Prudential Plc has agreed to acquire a majority stake in Bharti Life Insurance.{{Cite web |title=Prudential plans to acquire 75% stake in Bharti Life Insurance |url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/prudential-plans-acquire-75-stake-bharti-life-insurance-2026-05-17/ |website=Reuters}} A year earlier, in 2022, Bharti Airtel initiated its 5G rollout in India and secured a US$1 billion investment from Google.{{Cite web |last=Saha |first=Sneha |date=2022-08-29 |title=Airtel 5G services in India will start rolling out from October, confirms chairman Sunil Mittal |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/technology/news/story/airtel-5g-services-in-india-will-start-rolling-out-from-october-confirms-chairman-sunil-mittal-1993879-2022-08-29 |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=India Today |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Billionaire Sunil Mittal’s Airtel, Partners To Invest $1 Billion In Indian Data Center Projects |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/yessarrosendar/2026/03/31/billionaire-sunil-mittals-airtel-partners-to-invest-1-billion-in-indian-data-center-projects/}} In 2023, [[Brookfield Asset Management|Brookfield]] and Bharti Enterprises closed a deal, valued at approximately ₹5,000 crore, for four marquee commercial properties, including Worldmark assets located in [[Delhi Aerocity metro station|Delhi Aerocity]] and [[Gurgaon|Gurugram]].{{Cite web |last=Service |first=Express News |date=2023-05-02 |title=Brookfield closes Rs 5,000 crore realty deal with Bharti Enterprises |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/business/2023/May/01/brookfield-closes-rs-5000-crore-realty-deal-with-bharti-enterprises-2571311.html |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}} In 2024, Bharti Hexacom was listed through a ₹4,275-crore IPO.{{Cite web |date=2024-04-12 |title=Bharti Hexacom shares make a strong D-St debut; stock lists at 32% premium - CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/bharti-hexacom-ipo-listing-today-gmp-details-share-price-band-debuts-at-premium-issue-price-buy-sell-hold-19395692.htm |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=CNBCTV18 |language=en}} The same year, Mittal's Bharti Televentures UK acquired a 24.95% stake in the [[BT Group|BT Group Plc]]. In 2025, Bharti emerged as the second-largest shareholder in Sundrop Brands, a listed FMCG entity formed following the combination of Sundrop Brands Limited and Del Monte Foods, India.'''{{Cite web |title=Samara, Convergent-backed Agro Tech to buy Bharti-Del Monte JV |url=https://www.vccircle.com/samaraconvergent-backed-agro-tech-to-buy-bharti-del-monte-jv |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=VCCircle |language=en-US}}''' In March 2026, Sunil Bharti Mittal announced that he will transition from his role as Chairman of Airtel Africa in July 2026.{{Cite web |last=Fernandes |first=Jocelyn |date=2026-03-25 |title=Sunil Mittal to step down as Airtel Africa chair in July; to be succeeded by Gopal Vittal {{!}} Company Business News |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/sunil-mittal-to-step-down-as-airtel-africa-chair-in-july-to-be-succeeded-by-gopal-vittal-11774426351776.html |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=mint |language=en}} == Philanthropy == In 2000, Mittal established the Bharti Airtel Foundation (formerly the Bharti Foundation). The Foundation's primary initiatives include the Satya Bharti School Program, which manages 155 rural schools,{{cite web |author=Suzanne McGee |date=30 November 2009 |title=The 25 Best Givers |url=http://online.barrons.com/article/SB125935466529866955.html |access-date=1 April 2010 |work=Barron's}} and the Quality Support Program, which works with 1,100 government schools.{{Cite web |title=Bharti family pledges ₹7,000 crore to philanthropy |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/special/bharti-family-pledges-8377;7000-crore-to-philanthropy/48727/1 |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=www.forbesindia.com |language=en}} In 2024, it introduced TheTeacherApp, a free-for-life digital platform for teacher's professional development platform for educators and launched a Bharti Airtel Scholarship Programme for students from diverse socio-economic backgrounds, pursuing technology-focused engineering courses at the [[National Institutional Ranking Framework|NIRF]]-ranked engineering colleges. Through the foundation, Mittal has funded and partnered with several higher education institutions, including the [[Indian Institutes of Technology]] in Delhi and Mumbai, the [[Indian School of Business]], Plaksha University, Anant University, Chanakya University, the School of Ultimate Leadership (SOUL) and the [[University of Cambridge]].{{Cite web |title=Sunil Bharti Mittal - Creating Emerging Markets - Harvard Business School |url=https://www.hbs.edu/creating-emerging-markets/interviews/Pages/profile.aspx?profile=smittal |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=www.hbs.edu}} == Personal life == Sunil is married to Nyna Mittal, who is involved in philanthropic work focusing on education.{{cite web |last1=Avantika |date=12 April 2019 |title=These billionaire wives are perfect combination of beauty and brains |url=https://in.news.yahoo.com/billionaire-wives-india-perfect-combination-slideshow-wp-160059230/photo-p-nyna-mittal-married-founder-photo-160059673.html |access-date=13 October 2020 |website=in.news.yahoo.com |language=en-IN}} They have three children: a daughter, Eiesha Bharti Pasricha,{{cite news |last1=MacDonald |first1=Hugo |title=This Stunning London House Is the Perfect Place to Put Down Family Roots |url=https://www.architecturaldigest.com/story/this-stunning-london-house-is-the-perfect-place-to-put-down-family-roots |access-date=13 October 2020 |work=Architectural Digest |language=en-us}}{{cite news |last1=Shinner |first1=Josh |date=November 2019 |title=My Life, My Style |url=https://www.magzter.com/article/Fashion/Harpers-Bazaar-Malaysia/My-Life-My-Style |access-date=13 October 2020 |work=Harper's Bazaar Malaysia |language=en}} and twin sons, Kavin Bharti Mittal and Shravin Bharti Mittal. Sunil Bharti Mittal (born 23 October 1957) is an Indian entrepreneur and philanthropist. He is the Founder and Chairman of Bharti Enterprises, a conglomerate with interests in telecommunications, satellite communications, digital infrastructure, financial services, real estate, and hospitality. Its flagship company, Bharti Airtel, operates in 17 countries across India, South Asia and Africa and is the world's second-largest mobile operator by subscriber base. In 2024, Bharti Airtel became the first Indian company of its generation to reach a market capitalisation of US$100 billion.
Mittal also serves as the Co-Chairman of Eutelsat and is a Director on the board of BT Group Plc.
He has held various roles in several business and industry bodies. He was the Chaiman of the International Chamber of Commerce from 2016 to 2018 and the GSM Association from 2017 to 2018. Between 2009 and 2021, he served as a trustee of the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. During India's G20 presidency in 2023, he chaired the B20 Action Council on African Economic Integration. His additional board and advisory roles include membership in the World Economic Forum's International Business Council, Hakluyt's International Advisory Board, and the Global Board of Advisors at the Council on Foreign Relations. He has previously served on the boards of Unilever, Standard Chartered, and SoftBank Corp.
Mittal currently holds Co-Chair positions at the India-UK CEO Forum and is a Co-Anchor of the ICT and Emerging Technologies & Digital Infrastructure working group of the India–US CEO Forum. Earlier, he was the President of the Confederation of Indian Industry (2007–2008) and a member of the Prime Minister of India's Council on Trade and Industry (2004–2014). He was awarded the Padma Bhushan by the Government of India in 2007. In 2024, he was appointed an honorary Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire (KBE) by H.M. King Charles III, becoming the first Indian citizen to receive the honour from the King.
